news.title: Xabi Alonso on 'competitive monster' Jordan Henderson and Chelsea absentees
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has described Jordan Henderson as a 'competitive monster' after handing the midfielder his Chelsea debut at Brentford and explained why Reece James and Joao Pedro are absent this evening. Henderson joined the Blues on a free transfer this summer, but his Blues bow has been delayed due to the broken arm he sustained while away with England at this summer's FIFA World Cup. The 36-year-old has diligently undertaken his recovery at Cobham over the past six weeks and is now ready to make his Chelsea debut – and it comes against the club with whom he spent the previous campaign. On including Henderson in his side against Brentford, Alonso said: ‘The Premier League is about competing and Jordan is a competitive monster. 'I’m sure he will help the team with his quality, his game intelligence and the communication he has. We’re happy to have him back.' Alonso has been unable to call upon several players at the Gtech Community Stadium, with James and Joao Pedro joining Marco Palestra, Moises Caicedo and Emmanuel Emegha on the sidelines. 'Reece picked up a little injury in the last game against Hull and was feeling short in his recovery,' Alonso explained ahead of tonight's game. 'Joao we tried, but we expect to use the international break for him to be back in the next game against Bournemouth.' The Brazilian's absence means Danny Welbeck makes his full Premier League debut for the Blues, and will form part of an attack that includes Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. 'You need to adapt to the qualities of the players and get the benefit of what they do well,' Alonso explained when asked what Welbeck will offer as part of our front three. 'We know Danny is a reference and links very well. He is intelligent and knows where to play, and if we have a front three that works well it will be better for the team.'

news.title: Jordan Henderson on making his Chelsea debut at Brentford
news.body_en: Jordan Henderson has had to wait patiently to make his Chelsea debut. But having recovered from injury, the 36-year-old is in from the start against Brentford tonight and ready to make his mark. Henderson, who spent last season with the Bees, signed for the Blues earlier in the summer on a free transfer. However, having broken his arm while away with England at the FIFA World Cup, his first outing in Blue has been delayed. Tonight at the Gtech Community Stadium, Henderson will step out in a Chelsea shirt for the first time. And the midfielder is looking forward to introducing himself to the Blues faithful. 'Delighted to be back and have the feeling of getting onto the pitch,' Henderson explained ahead of this evening's Premier League clash with Brentford. 'It’s been a while, so I’m just excited to be back. 'It’s been a little frustrating [not being able to play], but I’ve tried to stay as fit as I can to be ready for this opportunity now. I’m just looking forward to it. 'It’s been good to settle in with the team over the last month, even though it’s been frustrating not playing games, but hopefully now I can get involved.' Henderson's illustrious career has seen him play hundreds of games at domestic level, in England and abroad. His last 34 came with Brentford during the 2025/26 campaign, with the England international impressing for the Bees before his departure and eventual switch to Stamford Bridge. It means that Henderson is well-versed in the threat Keith Andrews' side will pose tonight, and has outlined that the Blues will need to perform well to come away with a positive result. He said: 'They’re a fantastic team who can play with the ball, are good on transition and are good in behind. So it will be a very difficult game, as we know, so we’ve got to be 100 per cent to get anything from the game. 'But if we can play the way we know we can, we will cause them problems as well.'

news.title: Confirmed Chelsea line up vs Brentford
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has made five changes to his Chelsea team for today’s fixture away to Brentford, with a quartet of Blues handed their full Premier League debut. Pep Chavarria, Valentin Barco, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck are included in Alonso’s starting XI. Reece James and Joao Pedro are unavailable, while Malo Gusto, Jorrel Hato and Romeo Lavia drop to the bench. The other new face in the side from last weekend’s draw with Hull City is Maxence Lacroix, while Henderson's selection means he makes his Blues debut against the club he represented last season. The bench includes 16-year-old Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli for the first time in a competitive game. news.title: Key talking points from Sonia Bompastor's pre-Birmingham City press conference
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor faced the media at Cobham ahead of our Women's Super League clash with Birmingham City at Stamford Bridge, and here are the standout talking points from her press conference After a resounding 5-0 victory against Manchester United last Sunday, the head coach discussed the importance of a killer mindset, the strengths of our next opponents and her enjoyment of her role as Chelsea head coach. She also went into detail on the role of right wing-back Ellie Carpenter in the side and discussed what will be her 200th game as a manager on Saturday. 'I'm still having a great experience at Chelsea, and I'm loving every moment because I'm really passionate. 'After 200 games as a manager, I feel even more confident and more mature in terms of the way I manage the squad and my decisions every day. Every player and every manager comes to this league because they want to be challenged – that's also why I came here. 'I probably could have stayed longer in France and been more comfortable with winning more games, with not having maybe as much opposition, but that's not who I am. I want to be challenged. I want to find solutions when it's difficult, and this league is really good for that reason.' 'I've been talking a lot about mentality and mindsets. I think every team in this league has a lot of quality, really good individuals, but what sometimes makes the difference is your mentality and your mindset coming into training sessions every day and coming into the games. 'This mentality to want to hurt the team when you are playing against them makes the difference between having good players and the best players in the world. The main difference between our first game and the second was the intensity and the mindset we played with in the Man United game; I think it was quite clear. 'Coaching that is not always easy, but that's my job, and we are focusing on that a lot because I think we have enough quality in this team, so it's making sure we always bring the intensity into our games, but also the right mindset.' 'I think Ellie is a player who can play different positions in different systems. Right now, we are using her more as a right wing-back. That position gives her maybe a little bit more freedom because she knows she has players behind her who are defending, and we are keeping a better balance in the team. 'A lot of spaces were in that corridor during the last two games we played in, so that's why we were attacking that side. She has the ability to hurt teams in the space in behind the back line. 'She's quick, her ability with the ball is also improving a lot, and she's able to have really good crosses. She's able to score great goals when she comes into that position in the box. So that's something we are trying to use a lot because it's working, but we also have the opportunity to do that on the left side with Alyssa Thompson. 'She's also a really good profile for us to use and to, again, use the speed of them both behind the back line. So, yeah, we'll see.' 'They have the ability, with individuals and as a team, to have a lot of quality in terms of the defensive aspects, but also hurting teams in different ways. They are really well organised defensively as well. 'I watched their first two games and some of the games in preseason for Birmingham, and they have a lot of quality. Even if they lost their first game, the performances were good. So we need to be at our best tomorrow.' 'First and foremost, when you have some injuries and players are not available, you need to have this versatility. You need to find solutions when you are a manager. 'So I think it's good for me as a coach to sometimes talk to the players about being able to play in different positions, but also in terms of tactics, trying to help them understand different positions. So you do that a lot with the young players in the academy, but also in the first team at Chelsea with the young ones. 'I think we are lucky enough to also have experienced players who can play multiple positions, and it's good, especially when you get injuries, so you can still try to manage and find the right solutions to win the game.' Don't miss our huge London derby clash against Arsenal at Stamford Bridge! Secure your seat now...

news.title: Bompastor Press Conference 🎙️
Sonia Bompastor delivers positive injury update on key trio
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has confirmed that Nathalie Bjorn, Naomi Girma and Melvine Malard will all be available for selection when we take on Birmingham City at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea host the newly-promoted side tomorrow afternoon, with kick off scheduled for 12.45pm, and Bompastor will have extra resources to call upon. Bjorn was named on the substitutes' bench for our 5-0 win against Manchester United last weekend, but did not feature. Meanwhile, Girma and Malard were not in the squad. However, Bompastor says each of the trio is in contention to feature this time around. 'Nay is back in the group and will be with the group tomorrow for the game,' confirmed the Blues boss. 'Nat Bjorn is back, and Melvine Malard is also back in the squad. 'It's really important, really good and positive, especially as we are going to enter a period of three games in a week and six games in the next two weeks. 'It's really important to have as many players available as possible because I think if you want to maintain the intensity, you need to be able to rotate and have some fresh legs coming into every game.' Mayra Ramirez has also been absent from the squad in recent weeks and Bompastor gave an update on her availability too. 'Mayra is back in Colombia for personal reasons,' Bompastor explained. 'The club is supporting her in the best way possible and we are hoping to see her back with the squad and with the team soon.'

news.title: Alonso on Welbeck’s smooth adaptation and Henderson value
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has praised Danny Welbeck's immediate impact at Chelsea and highlighted the vital experience Jordan Henderson has brought to the Blues squad ahead of today’s Premier League clash at Brentford. Welbeck arrived at Stamford Bridge this summer from Brighton and Hove Albion to reinforce our frontline and add expertise from his many years playing in the Premier League. It is apparent from the words of his Chelsea team-mates that the 35-year-old has integrated seamlessly into the group off the pitch. On it, Welbeck has shown encouraging signs in his early appearances, which have included goals in both of our Carabao Cup fixtures so far. There is the possibility of Welbeck making his full Premier League debut for the Blues this evening at the Gtech Stadium. That is a decision for Alonso to make, but the Spaniard has been pleased with the striker's smooth adjustment to life at the Bridge ‘He has adapted very well,’ said Alonso. ‘There was no doubt about that. He has connected very well with the team. He knows what he has to do. ‘He has started a couple of games in the Carabao Cup, and the other day he was close to scoring one goal, so yeah, we are happy with Danny.’ With a demanding fixture list across multiple competitions, Alonso reiterated that every Chelsea player, including Welbeck, must remain prepared to step up when called upon. ‘It's about having a complete squad and about knowing that everyone is ready to play whenever they’re needed,’ he added. ‘You have to be ready. This is professional football, and you need to know when you are in, you need to perform.’ Our third consecutive London away game this season takes us to Henderson's previous home. The midfielder is yet to make his Blues bow following the arm injury he suffered at this summer’s World Cup, but Alonso has not ruled out the possibility of the 36-year-old featuring against his former club tonight. And our manager provided background on the reasons behind Henderson's signing in the summer: chiefly his ability to elevate standards on and off the ball. ‘We analysed it and we wanted to have a good balance between maturity, between experience, between talent, between energy. We have taken a step forward, and we have improved, I think, in that part. ‘Jordan has played an important role being a midfielder, with the impact that he can have with other players, but he has this quality and this personality to improve and to help other players as well. ‘We wanted to have a good balance and people who could add value for what they do and what could improve the other ones, and Jordan does it very well.’

news.title: Romeo Lavia on feeling free, taking responsibility and changing his Chelsea narrative
news.body_en: Romeo Lavia has thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea coaching staff for helping him overcome adversity and start this season strongly, as he looks to push himself to new levels on the pitch. The midfielder's Chelsea career, by his own admission, has been stop-start. Injuries have made it difficult for the Belgian to find his rhythm at Stamford Bridge, although when fully fit, supporters have seen the qualities he brings to the side. This season, Lavia has started our opening four Premier League fixtures under Xabi Alonso. He has impressed, looked sharp, and helped cover the absence of Moises Caicedo – the Ecuadorian's only minutes this term came as a second-half substitute against Brighton and Hove Albion. It's no surprise, then, that Lavia is feeling confident and has a renewed sense of purpose at Chelsea. He is determined to show everyone what he is truly capable of. ‘This season feels different because I'm in a different…let’s say mindset or space of mind,’ explained Lavia. ‘We've done a lot of work over the summer with all the people at the club to make sure that we could get everything that's happened before behind me. So far it's going well. I'm very happy and long may it continue. ‘To show up under the lights on the weekend is the last part of the puzzle; there is so much that goes on behind the scenes. It's the constant analysing of all the aspects that you want to tick off before being ready to play on the weekend. It's a big process, but we're doing well at the moment. ‘I've learned that you can always go further than you think you can. You can always push your limits, especially when you feel like everything is going against you. It's always so easy to just think about giving up, or think that no matter what you do, it's only going to go back to the same point where you started. ‘Luckily, with the help of my team-mates, the staff, everyone at the club and outside, the people close to me, we've been able to create a sort of bubble where you just concentrate on what you can control, and then everything will come out on top. ‘It's been a little bit stop-start since I've joined, so it's a bit frustrating, but the reason why I'm so excited about what's to come is that, whether it's in training or games, I feel the love from my team-mates. ‘I feel like they trust in me, which is then giving me the confidence to go and express myself without thinking about what's happened. That's something that really helps me.’ That love was evident when Lavia scored his first Chelsea goal earlier this season. He found the net in our 4-3 win over Brighton & Hove Albion at Stamford Bridge, sparking emotional celebrations as the rest of the players rushed to congratulate him in front of the home fans. ‘To be honest, when it first went in, I didn't really believe it because it's just been so long,’ the 22-year-old admits. ‘I had kind of lost that feeling of scoring, but thinking back, it was an amazing feeling. Then, straight away, all my team-mates grabbed me. So it was a very good moment to experience. ‘It was just a moment where I felt free, where it feels like all the work that you're putting in, you're getting the reward for it. It was a very good but very emotional moment at the same time, so I wanted to express it as much as possible with the fans. I really loved it. ‘Especially because I wanted to change the narrative. My first Premier League goal was against Chelsea, so I always felt like it was a bit strange. 'Then I've seen all my team-mates score at Stamford Bridge and the atmosphere that it would create, so I was waiting for it to be my turn. When it happened, I was just very happy and excited.’ Of course, it is for far more than that goal that his team-mates, the supporters and Alonso are so pleased to see Lavia back in the Chelsea midfield, with the quality of his performances this season making it seem like he has never been missing. If he was feeling any pressure to make up for lost time, he certainly hasn’t shown it. ‘Responsibility is something that has always been part of my game as well, to take responsibility and have some character,’ Romeo added. ‘I really like being in that position and also being at this club, having this responsibility. It's not even pressure; it's just like a privilege. So I'm actually living the dream. It's just like: “Okay, this is what you've been playing and training all these years for, so just go and enjoy it.”’

news.title: Chelsea FC transforms community football pitch in Ecuador
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club has completed the renovation of a community pitch in Guayaquil, Ecuador, as part of our global Can’t Tame Us campaign for the 2026/27 third kit launch, creating a renewed space for football, connection and community in one of the city’s most densely populated neighbourhoods. Located in Guasmo Norte, the futsal pitch is more than a place to play. Set among the homes and everyday life of the neighbourhood, it provides a shared outdoor space where children can kick a ball around, friends can compete, families can watch from the sidelines and neighbours can stop to talk. The renovation gives the community a refreshed place to come together through a shared love of sport, while helping to make football more accessible to the next generation. Click to shop the third kit now Ecuador is the country that gave us Moises Caicedo, the winner of our Men’s Player of the Year for the 2024/25 season, and Kendry Paez who has recently returned from a loan to join our Cobham Next Gen squad. Indeed, Guayaquil is Paez’s home city. The official opening of the pitch took place yesterday, with Ecuadorian singer Javier Neira, known for La Tri, in attendance, performing three songs. Influencers including Anthony Lencina, Camilo Balladares, Francisco Molestina, Israel Vera and Santiago Morales alongside members of the Chelsea family and local residents watched the celebrations as the renewed pitch was unveiled. The Guayaquil renovation is the third community facility to be refurbished this summer as part of Can’t Tame Us, with football’s generational appeal being used to bring communities together and encourage greater participation in the sport. The project follows the launch of facilities in São Paulo and in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, with thousands of fans visiting and using the renewed pitches. Across all three locations, the aim is simple: to create spaces where football can be played, shared and passed from one generation to the next; using the power of the game to bring people together and help communities thrive. Scott Fenton, Brand director at Chelsea FC, said: ‘Ecuador has a special connection with Chelsea and has produced incredible players such as Moises Caicedo, and fantastic talents like Kendry Paez. We want to build on that connection by inspiring and empowering future generations of fans and young footballers, giving them the opportunity to discover their potential, develop their skills and dream big. This community space is an important part of that commitment.’

news.title: FPL 2026/27: Chelsea Gameweek five
news.body_en: Chelsea have teamed up with Fantasy Football Scout to help bring you hints, tips and advice during the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season. Scout will be using their expertise to provide advice and gameweek tips which should prove useful in ensuring you win your mini-leagues. Here, we look at which of the Blues' players are must-haves, who the best value-for-money picks are, and why Morgan Rogers (£7.7m) is Chelsea’s most popular player this week. Cole Palmer (£9.7m) continues to show consistency, picking up his fourth attacking return of the season in the entertaining 2-2 draw against Hull City in Gameweek 4. Chelsea’s attack has scored a whopping 18 goals in six matches under Xabi Alonso. Our number 10 had three shots on goal and created three chances at Stamford Bridge - no Chelsea player could better that in Gameweek 4. Averaging nearly seven points per match, Cole is currently on course to surpass his best-ever Fantasy season of 244 points in 2023/24, where he racked up 22 goals and 13 assists. No player has been transferred in by more Fantasy managers than Morgan Rogers (£7.7m) ahead of the Gameweek 5 deadline. Nearly 500,000 people have moved to bring Chelsea’s summer signing into their team; he now sits in just under 40% of squads. Rogers is the only player to register an attacking return (three goals and one assist) in each of the first four Gameweeks. Against Hull last time out, the Englishman scored and claimed a share of the bonus points. Among Blues players, Rogers ranks first for chances created (10) and passes into the penalty box (11). This demonstrates his strong assist potential ahead of Friday’s fixture against Brentford. In an Aston Villa shirt, the Chelsea number 17 netted twice against the Bees in the Premier League. Playing regularly at wing-back, Pedro Neto (£6.5m) has, in recent matches, scored the Blues’ second goal against Brighton and netted in the Carabao Cup, as well as hitting the post at Arsenal with an unfortunate first-half effort. No Blues player has registered more successful passes in the final third (50) than Neto. The Portugal international is one to watch as he is the cheapest Blues attacker in FPL to have started a league game so far. In goal, Emi Martinez (£5.0m) has picked up a save point in each of his three appearances for the club, racking up 15 saves in all. No goalkeeper has made more saves in that time. When the Blues begin keeping clean sheets, Martinez’s ceiling will be high. At £5.0m, he is cheaper than most other goalkeepers playing for top-four contending teams. As usual, Erling Haaland (£15.5m) is a key contender in the captaincy conversation ahead of Manchester City’s home fixture against Sunderland. The Norwegian has racked up some impressive underlying numbers, ranking first among all players for shots (16), shots on target (9) and big chances (7). Haaland has scored in three consecutive Gameweeks, claiming the maximum three bonus points on each occasion. The Black Cats have conceded in both their away matches this season. Elsewhere, Morgan Gibbs-White (£8.0m) is an intriguing option against Coventry City. The English midfielder has registered three attacking returns in the last three Gameweeks and takes penalties for Nottingham Forest. A home fixture against bottom-of-the-table Coventry, who conceded five goals last time out, looks primed for attacking returns. No player has created more big chances (4) so far this season than Gibbs-White, who has been bought by over 370,000 Fantasy managers.

news.title: Chelsea FC Women launches best-in-class Player Maternity Policy as part of new family-friendly player care framework
news.body_en: Enhanced policy provides fully paid leave, personalised pregnancy support and dedicated return-to-play medical care, alongside new adoption, parental leave and fertility support. Chelsea FC Women (CFCW) has today announced a new, enhanced suite of family-friendly policies designed to provide our players with greater financial security, personalised care and comprehensive support through pregnancy, parenthood and other family-building journeys, as the club continues our ambition to set the standard for player care in women’s football. Chelsea FC has always been proud to offer industry-leading maternity support, but players face a unique challenge in balancing peak physical performance on the pitch with the demands of pregnancy, post-partum recovery and balancing motherhood with their return to play. We are therefore setting out a new suite of policies to provide wraparound, tailored support for our players that will better help them navigate starting a family. The centrepiece of the new framework is the club’s Player Maternity Policy, offering personalised support throughout pregnancy and dedicated medical care to support each player’s individual return to professional football. The policy has been developed to give players greater financial security and confidence planning for parenthood, recognises that every player’s journey is different, while ensuring their health and wellbeing remain the priority throughout pregnancy and their transition back to elite sport. The club’s enhanced approach includes: Personalised support throughout pregnancy, with the right to access private scans and delivery options Post-partum recovery support, led by the club’s industry-leading experts covering physical, mental and emotional aspects of postnatal health Financial support for a partner or nanny to travel to away fixtures up to one year after a player’s return to play, to ensure those early months of returning to play post-delivery are fully supported Enhanced adoption and parental leave policies, recognising that there is no single path to becoming a parent Subsidised childcare, a contribution to childcare costs when a player returns to rehab or training These policies follow our recently announced partnership with Fertility Plus, which includes the creation of a Player Value in Kind Fund to financially support players exploring their fertility and family-building options. The breadth of policies has been comprehensively reviewed and revised as part of CFCW’s pursuit to be never done challenging ourself and never done pushing for progress. Most recently this ambition has been brought to life with all of the team’s Barclays Women’s Super League matches now being played at Stamford Bridge, through working with industry-leading partners delivering campaign-winning work and enhancing policies to offer our players the very best care, not only on the pitch, but in all areas of life and at every stage of their careers. Aki Mandhar, Chief Executive Officer for Chelsea FC Women, said: ‘There is no single path to becoming a parent, and our responsibility is to ensure our players have access to the support, security and care they deserve, whatever their individual journey looks like. Our enhanced Player Maternity Policy, alongside our adoption, parental leave and fertility support, is designed to give our players confidence that they will be supported throughout their careers with us.’ Phil Radley, Sporting Director for Chelsea FC Women, added: ‘We are proud of the progress we are making, but we are never done looking for ways to do more. Our ambition is to build the best women’s sports organisation in the world; one that truly values its players and gives them everything they need to thrive – both as athletes and as people.’

news.title: London's Finest vs The Bees 🐝
Alonso confident there’s ‘more to come’ from Cole Palmer
news.body_en: Cole Palmer has started the season in excellent form and Xabi Alonso believes our No10 can reach even greater heights if he keeps enjoying his football. Palmer was outstanding in his first two campaigns at Stamford Bridge, but injury made it difficult for him to replicate that level of performance in 2025/26. He didn’t go to the FIFA World Cup this summer, and the break afforded him a chance to rest and reset. It has served Palmer well, with the attacker already finding the net four times and registering two assists. We will find out today if Palmer is back in the England fold, but for now Alonso has urged him to just keep playing with a smile on his face. ‘I think there's some more to come from Cole,’ said Alonso. ‘I'm very happy with Cole. The way he has prepared since the first day of pre-season, he's been there. He has shown this desire to enjoy his game. ‘What he wants is to enjoy his game, to have this good feeling on the pitch, to have this connection with players around. If he gets that, the rest will come. England will come, winning more games will come. ‘That will come naturally because he's a top-level player and that's the main thing, for him to feel good.’ Alonso has not been working with Palmer for long, but he can already tell he has a unique personality that will continue to stand him in good stead. ‘I've been here for two months. Day by day I get to know the players better, and I get to know Cole better, and Cole gets to know me better. ‘It’s about having connection, having contact, and Cole is a special man.’

news.title: Brentford vs Chelsea: All you need to know
news.body_en: Chelsea’s localised start to the season on all fronts continues with a seventh match in succession played in the capital. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton preview our trip to Brentford’s Gtech Community Stadium. The 8pm Friday kick-off will also be the Blues’ last west London derby on the road of the current league campaign. End-to-end 2-2 draws at the weekend prompted both managers to wistfully wish for a ‘boring’ game – 51 goals have already been scored in matches across all competitions involving the west London pair. The unbeaten Bees have drawn three on the spin in the top flight, but won 2-1 at Reading in midweek to reach the last 16 of the Carabao Cup. Chelsea's ball was already in the round four bowl so Xabi Alonso had a free week to prepare his players for this fixture after Saturday’s 2-2 home draw with Hull. Alonso and Keith Andrews will lock horns in the technical area for the first time, but at Euro 2012 they vied for midfield supremacy as Spain beat the Republic of Ireland 4-0, a win in which Chelsea’s Fernando Torres scored twice. In this same fixture last season at the Gtech, the Blues came from behind to lead, but conceded a last-gasp equaliser for 2-2 and a share of the spoils. Either club claiming all three points would lift them to third place in the table going into the weekend action. After that comes FIFA’s three-week, four-match international break, with club football resuming on 10 October, when Chelsea host Bournemouth. Alonso confirmed that Joao Pedro and Reece James, along with the whole of his Chelsea squad, remain in contention to face Brentford. There were concerns over Joao Pedro after the striker withdrew from the Brazil squad for the upcoming international break, and James as he missed the start of training on Tuesday. ‘In terms of injuries and in terms of the squad, we are having the last training session on Friday so no-one is ruled out for us,’ he explained in his pre-match press conference. ‘So I prefer to be cautious and we will wait to take the final decision on every player. We will see if Joao is ready to play, it’s a possibility. For Reece, it was just a decision for Tuesday and we see his development and  we will decide.’ It was a similar story when Alonso discussed the potential return from injury of Moises Caicedo, Marco Palestra and Jordan Henderson. ‘Moises is getting closer and we will take the final decision on the team and on the squad that is coming to Brentford. Before the players know we need to assess all the positions with the last training and we will make the decision for the game.’ One of Chelsea’s most memorable trips to Maine Road came in a rare Friday night match in early May 1984, Match Of The Day coverage of the tussle with Manchester City vying with That’s My Boy on ITV for the viewing public’s attention. It was the first time a Division Two match had been given the BBC’s live treatment and already-promoted Chelsea struck twice in six minutes to show why they and not the Cityzens were rejoining the elite. Fast forward eight years to 11 December 1992 and a dour 0-0 between Middlesbrough and Chelsea meant Teesside hosted the first Friday night match in Premier League history. The August 2002 clash between the Blues and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge was brought forward to the end of the working week to avoid Notting Hill Carnival congestion. The hosts twice led though William Gallas then Boudewijn Zenden, but the Mancunians levelled on each occasion and an entertaining game finished 2-2. Friday 12 May 2017 at West Bromwich Albion proved a red letter day in the Black Country for the Blues. The hosts doggedly held out until Michy Batshuayi’s opportunistic winner and at the final whistle the title-winning celebrations were lengthy and joyful. Last season, the same night of the week served up substantial away wins on two fronts – 5-1 at West Ham United in the league and 4-0 at Hull City in the FA Cup. Those were the Blues’ second and third-highest scores of the season and Pedro Neto notched four across the two games. Prior to that, a Marc Cucurella goal without reply had claimed all three points at home to Man Utd in May 2025, making the 3-0 at Brighton & Hove Albion two months earlier our most recent Friday loss. No Premier League goalkeeper has made more saves this season than Chelsea’s Emi Martinez or Brentford’s Caoimhin Kelleher (both 15). The Blues have recorded and sustained the joint-most shots on target in the top flight, 24 for and 26 against. Chelsea have broken the deadlock in the opening seven minutes of all four Premier League fixtures to date – in the first minute at Fulham, fourth at home to Brighton, second at Arsenal and seventh against Hull. Last weekend, Cole Palmer marked his 100th Premier League appearance with his 71st goal contribution (49 goals, 22 assists). Only Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink produced more in his first century for the Blues. Joao Pedro has already set up and scored a goal in the same top-flight game three times this season, matching his best performance in any campaign in England. The Bees have opened the scoring in each of their past three league games, and conceded the equaliser on each occasion.

news.title: Alonso on ‘complete’ Brentford’s tough test
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso is well aware of the difficult task awaiting his Chelsea team when we play Brentford on Friday evening, and our manager has been quick to point out that our opponents carry many threats beyond the obvious. After two wins and a draw from our opening four Premier League games, the Blues sit sixth in the table at this early stage of the season. A short distance across west London, the Bees remain undefeated, one point and one place below us in the standings. Much has been made of Brentford’s prowess at set-pieces and in transitions under manager Keith Andrews, but Alonso insists there is much more to their game. That makes them a dangerous opponent, especially on home soil at the Gtech Community Stadium, as we found out in our 2-2 draw there last September. ‘They do those things very well, but they do other things, not just the transition, not just the set-pieces,’ said the Chelsea manager. ‘It's a club that have developed their project and the game very well. They are very complete in many aspects, with the ball, without the ball. ‘And playing there, you see the numbers and they have great strength playing at home, so it's going to be a big challenge. I saw the game from last year, you learn from everything, and tomorrow is going to be a big test for us.’ Of course, we carry our own threat from set-pieces, with only Brighton & Hove Albion having scored from those situations more times than the Blues so far in 2026/27. That has been helped by the addition of Austin MacPhee to Alonso’s staff as set-piece coach for this season. ‘We want to have top specialists in each area in terms of the offensive part, defensive and set-pieces, and Austin has this great experience in the Premier League,’ added Xabi. ‘He's helping us a lot and we have trained like we always do to try to prepare for the games and knowing what we are facing tomorrow.’ At this stage of the season it is too soon to tell how the chips will fall in terms of the Premier League title race and beyond, even as the picture begins to take shape at Stamford Bridge and at grounds across the country. That is very much at the front of Alonso’s mind when he considers where his team stands so far. ‘It's too early to tell. For sure, there are Arsenal, Man City, they have won all the games so far, but there are still so many games. ‘I knew, but once you live it, you realise how tough each game is, how tough it is to win in the Premier League. You can't take any game for granted. ‘You need to give your best level because you get punished whenever you are not, and we have experienced that. But I think that there will be good moments for all the teams and bad moments for all the teams.’ Hopefully Friday night’s game will be one of the good moments for Chelsea, allowing us to bring three points back across west London to Stamford Bridge.

Training ahead of Brentford!
Internationals: England Women Under-20s exit World Cup
news.body_en: England's Young Lionesses were knocked out of the Women's Under 20-World Cup with a 3-0 defeat to Nigeria in Poland. Lydia Bedford's side had progressed through a difficult group with wins over Brazil and Tanzania and a draw with Canada. The Round of 16 saw them face Nigeria, with Blues youngsters Lola Brown, Katie Cox, Chloe Sarwie and Vera Jones all named in the starting XI, and Eva Hendle an unused substitute. An early opener from Tosin Rafiu saw the Lionesses 1-0 down after eight minutes. Aston Villa's Rachel Matlby, who had been prolific throughout the tournament, missed a penalty on the half-hour mark that would have seen England draw level. There were bright moments from the Blues stars as goalscorer Mamudu was denied by an excellent recovery tackle from Sarwie in the second half, and Brown then saw her half-volleyed effort well saved by goalkeeper Christiana Uzoma. Yet it wasn't to be, and second-half strikes from Janet Akekoromowei and Mary Mamudu were enough to see Nigeria progress to the last eight.

news.title: Alonso: We need to find the right balance and mentality
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso is sure that his Chelsea team will find the right balance between attack and defence in time, highlighting mentality and adaptability as the keys to adding clean sheets to our free-scoring form in front of goal. There is no questioning the potent attacking threat the Blues have posed to opponents so far this season under Alonso’s leadership, having scored 18 goals across our opening six fixtures in all competitions. However, after some thrilling high-scoring victories, the goals conceded at the other end cost us two points when Hull City came from behind to secure a draw at Stamford Bridge last week. As we prepare to take on Brentford in our next game on Friday, our manager made clear it is an area he and his players are working hard on improving. ‘It's obvious that in defence we can do better,’ he said. ‘In attack, we are doing well, but we need to find the right balance between the defence and the attack to not concede that many goals. ‘It's for sure clear and I'm sure that we will do it. Everything takes time. We have had circumstances that haven't allowed us to create the stability that we want, but once we get it, I think that we will be more solid.’ Alonso also dismissed any suggestion it is an issue purely for the defenders to worry about, calling for focus in all moments from every Chelsea player at the Gtech Community Stadium tomorrow evening, so we can cope with any circumstances that can arise during the intensity of a Premier League match. ‘The defence is all the team,’ the Spaniard continued. ‘It's not just the back four or the back five, it's about the team. ‘It's how we compete, how we adapt to different moments. When we take the lead or when the game is even, we need to have the same mentality to be competing in different moments. ‘We know that in the Premier League it is very difficult to control the whole game, but to be able to adapt and to feel that awareness that is needed is very important. ‘We have had four or five weeks since we started. This is going to be the seventh game in this block. It's an important one because it's before the international break, because it's in the Premier League, because it's away against Brentford who are tough. So we will have to play a high-demand game.’

news.title: Alonso Press Conference 🎙️
Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Brentford
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso confirmed that Joao Pedro and Reece James, along with the whole of his Chelsea squad, remain in contention to face Brentford going into matchday. The Blues make the short trip across west London to take on Brentford in the Premier League’s Friday night kick-off, hoping to get back to winning ways after last week’s 2-2 draw with Hull City at Stamford Bridge. There were concerns over Joao Pedro after the striker withdrew from the Brazil squad for the upcoming international break, and James as he missed the start of training on Tuesday. However, Alonso insists they have not been ruled out of our next match. ‘In terms of injuries and in terms of the squad we are having the last training session tomorrow so no-one is ruled out for us for Friday,’ he explained. ‘So I prefer to be cautious and we will wait until tomorrow to take the final decision on every player. We will see tomorrow if Joao is ready to play, it’s a possibility. ‘For Reece, it was just a decision for Tuesday and we see his development and tomorrow we will decide.’ Our manager also hinted that there is a chance that Moises Caicedo could return to the matchday squad, with the midfielder having been restricted to just a brief appearance against Brighton & Hove Albion so far this season. ‘He’s getting closer and tomorrow we will take the final decision on the team and on the squad that is coming to Brentford.’ It was a similar response when Alonso was asked in his pre-match press conference if Marco Palestra or Jordan Henderson could be fit enough to make their Chelsea debuts at the Gtech Community Stadium, underlining that he will continue to monitor his options right up until it comes to the moment to name his team on Friday. ‘Tomorrow is the final decision,' he added. 'Sorry to repeat myself, but before the players know we need to assess all the positions with the last training and tomorrow we will make the decision for the game in Brentford.’

PGA South League report: Brighton 1-2 Chelsea Women’s Under-18s
news.body_en: Chelsea Women's Under-18s maintained their unbeaten start to the league campaign with a 2-1 victory away at Brighton. The Blues took an early lead through Chelsea N'Drin's penalty before the hosts levelled after the interval. Keira Johnson (pictured top) then struck in stoppage time to secure all three points for Leanne Champ's side. Chelsea had 60 per cent possession and created 25 attempts, with 14 on target, as we battled well against a tough Brighton side. The fixture also provided an opportunity for players returning from England Women's Under-17s activity against Finland to feature again. Chelsea made a positive start and were rewarded with the opening goal after just three minutes. Patient build-up play across the back line allowed Gabi Storey to step forward with the ball and play beyond the Brighton midfield. Rebekah Pierce flicked the ball on, allowing N'Drin to use her pace to run past the Brighton centre-backs. The Brighton goalkeeper came off her line and brought down the forward, leaving the referee no option but to point to the spot. N'Drin took responsibility and converted with power and placement across the goal. The Blues continued to work hard against a tough Brighton side, creating opportunities while managing the hosts' threat. Brighton drew level after 64 minutes when a Chelsea attempt to play into midfield was intercepted. The hosts worked the ball to a winger who had moved inside, and she beat two Chelsea players before striking powerfully from around 20 yards. Her effort dipped underneath the crossbar to bring the scores level. Chelsea responded and continued to create chances, with Sophie Leach introduced for Sadie Gregory on the hour mark and Annie Boichat replacing Tess Finn at the same time. Stevie Sinclair had also come on for captain Belle Sullivan at half-time, while Jahyma Putman replaced Carla Gardiner. The decisive moment arrived in the second minute of added time. Leach, Zoe Ciccardini and Johnson combined during the build-up before a Brighton defender stepped in to challenge Johnson. Good positioning from Elise Christian allowed Chelsea to regain possession on the left. Christian drove forward into the space in front of her and, approaching the edge of the penalty area, slipped a perfectly weighted pass through to Johnson. The midfielder finished first time with her left foot across goal to secure a dramatic late victory. Chelsea remain unbeaten in the PGA South League, with 12 points from four fixtures. The Blues have scored 20 goals and conceded just two during our opening four league matches. Chelsea now welcome Arsenal Under-21s to Kingsmeadow for our first fixture of the season at the stadium on Sunday 20 September. Kick-off is at 7.30pm and admission is free. news.title: Chelsea FC announces ownership transition
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club today announced affiliates of Clearlake Capital Group, L.P. (“Clearlake”) will acquire the ownership interest of Todd Boehly. Hansjörg Wyss will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group. As part of the transition, Clearlake will also acquire Mark Walter’s ownership interest and therefore acquire full control of the Club. In 2022, Todd Boehly and Clearlake joined together to lead the historic acquisition of Chelsea – successfully navigating an unprecedented period of uncertainty imposed by outside political events – and Todd organised his chairmanship with an unwavering commitment to this ownership group’s fundamental belief that the supporters are at the heart of everything the Club does. The owners have worked together with the shared objective of building a sustainable foundation for long-term sporting success. Under their joint ownership, substantial investment has been made across the men's and women's senior and youth squads, Chelsea’s training facilities at Cobham, medical and player-support resources, Academy development and pathways, and the sporting and business leadership of the Club. Todd Boehly now leaves his role as Chairman with Chelsea well positioned for the next phase of development. The progress made over the past four years reflects the shared commitment of Clearlake, Boehly and the wider ownership group and the leadership, staff, coaches and players at Chelsea. Clearlake intends to continue building on the strategic course the Club is now on and realising the ambition that the ownership group has developed together. Todd Boehly said, 'It has been an honour to serve as Chairman of Chelsea Football Club. I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the Club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans. I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the Club. I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake’s leadership.' Behdad Eghbali and José E. Feliciano, co-founders of Clearlake Capital, said, 'Todd has been an important partner throughout our ownership of Chelsea, and we thank him for his time and contribution as Chairman. He will always be a part of the Chelsea story and family. Clearlake has served as Chelsea’s majority owner since 2022, and as we move to full control our focus is to continue investing in the Club’s infrastructure, sporting performance, player development and delivering long-term success for Chelsea and the Club’s supporters.' There will be no changes to the day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the Club. Evercore (NYSE: EVR) is serving as lead financial advisor on the transaction, with the Evercore team led by Simon Robey. The Raine Group, BDT&MSD Partners, and BofA Securities are serving as financial advisors to Clearlake. Sidley Austin LLP is serving as legal advisor to Clearlake and the Club. Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC is serving as financial advisor and Latham & Watkins LLP as lead legal advisor to the sellers, with additional advice provided to Mark Walter by Winston Taylor LLP. Macfarlanes LLP is serving as legal advisor to Hansjörg Wyss.

Becky Spencer recounts Jamaica's odds-defying 2023 World Cup campaign
news.body_en: Goalkeeper Becky Spencer brought a wealth of experience with her when she joined Chelsea in 2025 for her second spell with the club, and she has one story to tell in particular that is fascinating to hear. Becky is a quiet character; never one to boast about her accomplishments. But ahead of Saturday’s match with Birmingham City – a club she made almost 50 appearances for across two separate spells – she chatted with us about her against-all-odds experience with Jamaica at the 2023 Women’s World Cup. The story itself is so incredible that it has been made into a film, directed by two-time Oscar winner Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy and Trish Dalton, which premiered at DOC NYC in August. For context, Jamaica – nicknamed the Reggae Girlz – had only been to one World Cup before 2023. They failed to qualify three times and did not enter twice before reaching the tournament in France in 2019. On that occasion, they went home with no points and a minus 11 goal difference, finishing bottom of the group. At this point, it’s important to introduce Jamaican music legend Bob Marley’s daughter Cedella to the story. The Jamaica Football Federation have disbanded the women’s team twice due to funding issues: in 2008 and again in 2016. In 2014, Cedella Marley released a single to raise cash for the team and secured sponsorship through the Bob Marley Foundation. In the build-up to the 2023 World Cup, the JFF once again said they were struggling to fund the women’s team and called on the Jamaican government for support. In desperation, midfielder Havana Solaun’s mother set up a crowdfunding page called “Reggae Girlz Rise Up” to get them to the tournament. It raised $50,000. That’s where Becky takes up the story… ‘I've got quite a few career highlights to be honest,’ she says. ‘But I would say being at the World Cup with Jamaica is definitely up there. ‘I don't really talk about the story a lot. But we had to have a GoFundMe to get us to Australia and New Zealand in 2023. Jamaica is a male-dominated type of country. The money and the decisions are dominated by men, and so they put the senior boys' team ahead of us. ‘We really defied the odds by qualifying. And then when we actually got there, we had the group of death, which was Brazil, France, and then we had Panama. We drew against France in the first game; it was 0-0. Bunny (Khadija Shaw) got sent off, and she's our biggest player in the team. ‘It was a real uphill battle, but I think as a group we knew that we were going to be able to do something. We had Panama in the next game, and we knew we had to win that game to at least get three points, so we won 1-0.’ Rebecca Spencer is the first Jamaican goalkeeper to keep 3 clean sheets at the World Cup 🧼🧹🇯🇲 0 - 0 🇧🇷📸: @mr_geniuz .#ReggaeGirlz #FIFAWomensWorldCup #FIFAWWC #JAMBRA #BeyondGreatness #JFF_Football pic.twitter.com/WtDAI1JOAG With their first four points at a World Cup already in the bag, Jamaica faced Brazil in the final match of the group stage. The eyes of the world were on legendary Brazilian striker Marta, knowing she would likely be appearing in her last major tournament on the world stage. Yet it was unfavoured Jamaica who would make the headlines. Spencer earned the Player of the Match award for facing eight shots on target and keeping a clean sheet, with the 0-0 draw enough to make history for the Reggae Girlz and knock Brazil out. ‘We had Brazil in the last match, and it was one of the most gruelling games,’ she says, before going on to describe what was going on behind the scenes. ‘I don't think I've ever concentrated so much in a game before. Everyone was just going for it; we defended literally for 90 minutes. We ended up drawing 0-0. So we got out of the group and into the round of 16. ‘Some of the girls were literally surviving off Uber Eats. The hotel that we were in wasn't good. There were no protein shakes, no recovery stuff. It just shows that if you've got a really strong bond within a team, that alone can take you a long way. ‘So you can only hope that if we did have all the rest of the stuff we needed, that we would actually be able to compete properly. ‘The outpouring of pride from Jamaica was amazing, and I think we showed the nation – and other nations who are struggling as well – that you can actually do it even if you don't have the resources.’ Jamaica were narrowly beaten in their first knockout round fixture, a 1-0 defeat at the hands of Colombia. Yet the team had won hearts and minds with their incredible story, and the result is what Becky describes as 'bigger than football'. ‘It was important to send another message home to Jamaica that we can achieve big things,’ she says. ‘And even if you don't have everything, you can still make it through. That’s the biggest message. Making it totally against all odds. It was honestly amazing, and we got a lot of support around the world as well. ‘I remember getting loads of messages from people in England being like, "We're Jamaica fans now because you lot are just brilliant underdogs!" and that’s exactly what we were – total underdogs. I had never been in that position before. I was just like, “Okay, this is what it's all about." That’s why it’s one of my biggest career highlights - it almost beats winning anything, to be honest. ‘We wanted the younger generation in Jamaica to be able to see a pathway. To be able to see people playing who are like them, so they know that they can do it as well. It’s bigger than football. It's about a cultural shift as well. It really was fantastic.’ Don't miss our huge London derby clash against Arsenal at Stamford Bridge! Secure your seat now...

news.title: Lifting the Lid with Levi Colwill
news.body_en: Levi Colwill answers our questions to take us behind the scenes at Cobham and fill us in on life off the pitch for the Chelsea defender. Who is the first player out to training? Who do you normally have lunch with at Cobham? Probably Welbs, Morgs, Cole, Reece, Hendo. The English boys mainly. After training, what’s the first thing you do when you get home? Sit on my sofa and put the TV on, put my feet up. Who do you sit next to when travelling on away trips? I suppose it's probably just with the English boys again. Who do you sit next to in the dressing room on a matchday? Last time I was next to Morgs and Jamie Gittens. Who is the biggest joker in the squad? Who is the loudest member of the squad? Probably Wes again, to be fair. Who would you say is the most active on social media that people should follow? Romeo Lavia. Yeah, it's Lav, for sure. Who do you call or message first after a match? I probably answer my parents, because they've probably text me saying something. There’s always a message from them already when I pick up my phone after a game, so it's probably them. Which outfield player do you think would be the best goalkeeper? Probably Wesley Fofana again. I feel like he's just a bundle of energy and he'd actually enjoy it. He's a bit crazy, like goalies! Which defender or midfielder would make the best striker? What is the one thing that has surprised you the most since you've been at Chelsea? That’s hard because I was just a kid when I joined, so it's going back a long way. Probably, growing up here and that, just the level of every age group and how it improves until you get to the first team. There's always improvements being made, so you can never rest on your laurels. So every step you make, you can never think you've done it, even now.
